correctness.rationale: The occupancy indicator covariance formula is exact. For \(m\le2\) the variance is a concave quadratic in a strictly increasing detection probability, allowing at most one peak. The separated-abundance construction gives \(m-1\) high points converging to \(1/4\) and intermediate low points converging to 0; nonzero integer-polynomial adjacent differences at a small transcendental epsilon force strict interior maxima. Exact rational witnesses for \(m=3\) and 55 independent exact-state dynamic-program comparisons were run successfully; the analytic proof, not finite tests, establishes arbitrarily many peaks.

originality.rationale: The variance formula itself and asymptotic urn oscillation are prior art. The assessed final novelty is the finite, cardinality-resolved sharp minimum three for two strict peaks, and a fully quantified constructive m-1 multiscale family with Bernoulli-height maxima and vanishing intervening valleys. Relevant inspected primary sources and indexed records do not state or imply this full conjunction, although broader historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Broader finite-occupancy literature might already contain cardinality-sharp strict variance peak theorems under a different name.

Full text of Heck–van Belle–Simberloff 1975 and Archibald–Knopfmacher–Prodinger 2006 was not accessible in this round; abstract-based comparisons do not establish not covering.
Independent historical-priority review has not been performed.

value.rationale: Variance of observed ecological richness versus sampling effort under known abundance probabilities is an intrinsic uncertainty measure. The sharp \(m=3\) threshold proves a nontrivial minimal structural boundary, while the \(m-1\)-scale construction establishes repeated uncertainty surges separated by nearly deterministic periods. The claim highlights a substantive limitation of single-peak uncertainty intuition, distinct from formula recomputation. Empirical richness estimates and sampling design may be affected, but practical transfer under dependence is not asserted.
